name: IEC subtracter (P-Q)
summary: IEC arithmetic element marked P-Q that subtracts word Q from word P, with borrow handling.
description: The subtracter qualifier is written P minus Q. Inputs are grouped as the P and Q words with binary weights and outputs give the difference, with borrow input and output terminals for cascading. TI's overview lists it with the adder and other arithmetic qualifiers.

Dedicated subtracter devices are uncommon; the function is often provided by an adder with an inverted input word or by an arithmetic logic unit. Functional diagrams and programmable logic documentation still use the P-Q element to state intent clearly.
The symbol does not say whether the result is signed or how negative results are represented. State that in the logic description.
readingNotes: P is the minuend and Q the subtrahend.
distinction: The Σ adder adds P and Q; an ALU may perform either under mode control.
